title: Eli Finds His Strength
moral: Everyone has unique strengths—focus on your own.

scenes.summary: Eli is a kind elephant who compares himself to others.

In a sunny jungle filled with tall trees, lived a young elephant named Eli.

Eli was kind and strong.

But there was one problem…

Eli always compared himself to others.

scenes.summary: Eli feels inadequate when he sees what others can do.
scenes.text:
“Look how fast I run!” said Milo the Monkey.

“Look how high I jump!” said Zara the Zebra.

Eli looked at himself.

“I’m not fast… I’m not jumpy…” he sighed.

scenes.summary: Eli becomes sad and withdraws from playing with others.
scenes.text:
Eli stopped playing.

He sat under a tree.

“I’m not as good as them,” he said.

scenes.image_prompt: sad elephant sitting alone under tree while others play, soft cartoon style

scenes.summary: Tomo helps Eli realize his own strength when a log blocks the path.
scenes.text:
Just then, Tomo the Tortoise walked by.

“Why are you sad?” he asked.

“I can’t do what others can,” Eli said.

Tomo smiled.

“Everyone is different,” he said.

“Let’s see what you can do.”

Nearby, a heavy log blocked the path.

“No one can move it,” said the animals.

Eli stepped forward.

“I can try,” he said.

He pushed with his strong trunk.

Push… push…

The log rolled away!
scenes.image_prompt: elephant pushing heavy log with strength while animals watch, colorful cartoon

scenes.summary: Eli gains confidence and embraces his own strengths.
scenes.text:
“Wow!” everyone cheered.

“Eli is so strong!”

Eli smiled.

“I didn’t know I could do that!”

Eli stood tall.

“I don’t need to be like others,” he said.

“I just need to be me.”

Everyone has their own strengths.

Don’t compare—celebrate yourself.

The End

story:
Eli the Elephant Who Compared Too Much

In a sunny jungle filled with tall trees, lived a young elephant named Eli.

Eli was kind and strong.

But there was one problem…

Eli always compared himself to others.

“Look how fast I run!” said Milo the Monkey.

“Look how high I jump!” said Zara the Zebra.

Eli looked at himself.

“I’m not fast… I’m not jumpy…” he sighed.

Eli stopped playing.

He sat under a tree.

“I’m not as good as them,” he said.

“I wish I were different.”

Just then, Tomo the Tortoise walked by.

“Why are you sad?” he asked.

“I can’t do what others can,” Eli said.

Tomo smiled.

“Everyone is different,” he said.

“Let’s see what you can do.”

Nearby, a heavy log blocked the path.

“No one can move it,” said the animals.

Eli stepped forward.

“I can try,” he said.

He pushed with his strong trunk.

Push… push…

The log rolled away!

“Wow!” everyone cheered.

“Eli is so strong!”

Eli smiled.

“I didn’t know I could do that!”

Eli stood tall.

“I don’t need to be like others,” he said.

“I just need to be me.”

Everyone has their own strengths.

Don’t compare—celebrate yourself.

The End
